newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hard for India to raise oil product price-minister.
newsitem.headline: Hard for India to raise oil product price-minister.

text.p: India's Finance Minister Palaniappan Chidambaram told Reuters Financial Television on Wednesday that it would be difficult to raise the domestic retail prices of petroleum products.

On Sunday, the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Chidambaram as telling the TVI Network that the government was considering raising the price of petroleum products to cover the burgeoning cost of petrol subsidies.
Chidambaram denied the report, saying such a move would be difficult after an increase in prices in July.
"I did not say that we will raise prices," he said.
"The government is considering various options. Just last July we raised petroleum prices, it is difficult for the government to raise prices again," he said.
Asked what other options existed, Chidambaram said: "There are difficult options...there seem to be various points of view."
In July, India increased petrol prices by 25 percent and prices for diesel, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), paraffin wax and fuel oil by 30 percent.
But it later halved the increase in the price of diesel after public outcry and nationwide protests.
The government reimburses oil firms for the difference between what they pay to import crude and what domestic refiners pay them.
Ministry officials estimate that the oil pool deficit is expected to touch 155 billion rupees in 1996/97 ending March 31, against 57 billion rupees the previous year.
